activities.name: Guided Visit — Alicante Tide Gauge, Spain's "Height Zero"
activities.location: Alicante Tide Gauge & Geodetic Station (IGN) — Muelle de Levante, Port of Alicante
activities.address: Muelle de Levante, Puerto de Alicante, 03001 Alicante, Spain
activities.description: Sponsored by Neobora. Extended networking morning with a guided visit to the historic Alicante Tide Gauge, organised by Spain's National Geographic Institute (IGN). IGN experts will walk us through its history and explain how the National Altimetric Reference — the origin of every official height in mainland Spain — was established here. Bus departs the hotel at 09:30, returning at 13:00.
highlights: Between 1870 and 1874, IGN surveyors read the sea level by hand on a tide staff in Alicante's port every day; the average became the Mean Sea Level in Alicante (NMMA).
That mean sea level is the origin of altitudes for mainland Spain — 2024 marked its 150th anniversary.
The reference benchmark NP1 is a bronze disc on the first step of Alicante City Hall, set at 3.4095 m above mean sea level.
Spain's first tide gauge started recording here in 1874; the current station, ALAC1 (the 'Fundamental Station of the Mediterranean'), was built from 1925.
From paper chart recorders and 1960s punched tape to today's angular encoders and radar sensors sending data to IGN in real time, every minute.
A permanent GNSS station on site monitors any ground or port movement — and, via GNSS reflectometry, can measure sea level from satellite signals bouncing off the water.
